who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane LV (variant-count) on rebuild-1115
what: blaze-lint's contract is that a rule is a pure function of one item's text and its Scope, and the cli keys each Lint unit by exactly that. `variant-count` needs a fact of the whole file (the enums and their counts), which the enum's unit has and the literal's unit does not. Nothing in the crate had a seam for a file-level fact, so `lint` alone would have found nothing across units without saying so, and the unit keys would not have moved when an enum gained a variant.
cost: about half the lane: designing the seam and its key before writing the rule
cause: the item-alone design had no place for a fact read across items of one file
whys: every earlier rule reads only its item; Scope is a fixed u64 bitfield; the cli's unit_source hashes only own bytes, holes and the scope key
class: a rule reading anything outside its item silently finds nothing, or leaves stale records, unless its read joins the unit's key
prevention: done: `Variants::gather` (one lex per file, capped tables) is the file's fact; `lint_in` takes it; `Variants::unit_key` is the unit's read of it, joined to the cli's unit_source only when a literal of the unit has an enum of its count; `lint` alone treats its unit as its whole file. Test `variant_count_reads_the_file_and_keys_the_unit`.
